transcript:
HEADER: 2026-10-20 16:00 PT | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Maya Chen, Diego Alvarez, Priya Nair (Redwood) — Liam O'Connor, Priya Singh, Ruth Park, Omar Al-Karim (Horizon)

AUTO-SUMMARY: Weekly pilot sync; focused on rollout sequencing, canary thresholds, and monitoring runbook ownership.

--- TRANSCRIPT ---
00:00 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
00:05 Liam O'Connor: Hey — Liam here. Priya and Ruth are on. Omar will join in a sec.
00:10 Diego Alvarez: Diego here, happy to dive into the perf numbers.
00:12 Priya Nair: Priya Nair, I'll cover runbook ops bits.
00:20 Maya Chen: Cool. goal for today: review week three metrics, lock down a sequenced rollout plan and agree on gating thresholds. if we can get owners for the runbook pieces that's ideal.
00:35 Ruth Park: Sounds good. we also want to make sure any quality regressions hit our product SLOs — Liam mentioned a 300ms p95 target, is that right?
00:40 Liam O'Connor: yeah, for interactive flows we really need p95 under ~300ms. batch/async can tolerate more.
00:45 Diego Alvarez: quick note: our hosted baseline for the model under the current config is averaging p95 ~320–350ms for their typical 1.2k token windows, but with prefix caching and a tighter batching config we can push that down around 280–300 on our staging hardware. actual numbers vary with token length distribution.
00:58 Priya Singh: those numbers would be great. the current pilot showed a few spikes last Thursday that caused UI timeouts.
01:05 Diego Alvarez: I pulled that trace — spike coincided with a big prompt set hitting the KV cache cold path, so you'll see extra latency. we have a mitigation: smaller warmup population and pre-populate KV for the top 50 queries.
01:20 Liam O'Connor: ok, pre-populate is doable — we'll need the script.
01:25 Maya Chen: Diego, can you add that to action items?
01:28 Diego Alvarez: yep — adding.
01:32 Priya Nair: high-level on rollout: Redwood proposes a sequenced plan — safety window (internal traffic only) -> external canary at 5% for 2h -> 20% for 6h with metrics gating -> 50% for 12h -> full cutover. each step has latency and regression thresholds.
01:52 Ruth Park: that sequencing sounds fine. question: what are the exact gating thresholds?
01:58 Diego Alvarez: proposed gates: p95 latency must not exceed baseline by more than 15% OR absolute p95 > 400ms triggers rollback; error rate (5xx/err) must stay under 0.5%; quality gating — we run the 50-prod prompts and expect <2% semantic regressions compared to baseline. if quality fails, rollback immediate.
02:20 Liam O'Connor: 400ms p95 is higher than our ask — we need 300ms. can that be tightened?
02:30 Diego Alvarez: short answer: for 100% traffic maybe, but during the 20–50% ramp we can likely hold 300–350ms if we enable aggressive caching and bump instance type for the Dedicated pool. there's a cost tradeoff.
02:45 Maya Chen: and that's the point — gap between latency and cost. we'll send a pricing delta for the dedicated pool ops to meet a 300ms p95 target.
02:55 Priya Singh: is that the Dedicated SKU or some autoscaling setting?
03:00 Maya Chen: pricing diff is mostly Dedicated reserved GPU type (higher throughput) vs hosted burst. Diego has notes.
03:05 Diego Alvarez: yes, the kernel/path we pick and quantization together drive the p95. We can also fallback to a lower-accuracy quantized variant if we hit tail issues — it's in the fallback matrix.
03:20 Omar Al-Karim: security question — when you say caching and pre-populate, does any user data get persisted outside our VPC? we have strict residency rules.
03:28 Priya Nair: by default on Dedicated we can enable local KV caching inside customer's VPC nodes. for hosted mode we use encrypted cache with TTLs and can be configured to not write persistent logs. we will share the security deck.
03:40 Omar Al-Karim: we need that in writing — KMS usage, whether keys are customer-managed, and audit log retention.
03:47 Maya Chen: action: Maya to share security artifact (SOC2 & KMS options).
03:52 Omar Al-Karim: thanks.
04:00 Ruth Park: about monitoring — what dashboards will we need to own? latency p50/p95/p99, error rates, model quality regressions, tokens per request, queue length?
04:10 Priya Nair: yes, and we'll add a custom 'semantic regression' metric from the eval harness. Redwood will provide the Grafana dashboard template (link in chat), with alert conditions mapped to pager channels.
04:25 Diego Alvarez: also recommend an anomaly detector on p99 tail; lots of issues hide there.
04:30 Priya Singh: who owns the runbook during the safety window?
04:35 Maya Chen: recommend RW SE on-call + Horizon SRE as primary for the safety window; Priya Nair will draft escalation steps.
04:40 Priya Nair: I'll draft the runbook: gating checks, triage steps, rollback automation (curl snippet to toggle traffic), and who to page.
04:50 Liam O'Connor: on quality gating: we'll provide 50 canonical prompts. Redwood will run them and share per-prompt diffs. can we automate an A/B pass for those during the 20% window?
04:58 Diego Alvarez: yes — Redwood will run an A/B evaluation, comparing baseline model vs new rollout. we'll compute precision/recall-ish metrics for semantic content (approx). note transcription caveat: automated semantic metrics are heuristic.
05:15 Ruth Park: acceptable, but we need a manual check for high-risk prompts (payment flows).
05:20 Maya Chen: we'll mark the payment flows as 'must-pass' and add a manual signoff.
05:25 Liam O'Connor: cool. next, fallback: you mentioned auto-fallback to lower-accuracy variant. how quickly does that switch?
05:32 Diego Alvarez: we can automate immediate fallback within 30s of trigger alert if the Abnormality matches configured rule. rollback to previous stable or to the smaller quantized variant, plus optionally route to regional cluster.
05:45 Priya Singh: regional routing — do we have EU vs US segregation?
05:48 Maya Chen: yes — model routing by region is supported. you can pin EU traffic to EU-only nodes for compliance.
05:54 Omar Al-Karim: we need to confirm data residency for logs too.
05:57 Maya Chen: noted. action item for Omar to document retention reqs.
06:05 Diego Alvarez: quick demo: uploaded a spreadsheet with the 24h tail numbers and the spike traces (link: https://redwood.app/drive/hz-pilot-24h). note the large cold-path at 14:12 yesterday.
06:20 Priya Nair: ok looking at it — I see the KV miss rate is ~18% during peak. we should tune the cache TTL for the frequent prefixes.
06:30 Liam O'Connor: what's the overhead of pre-populating 50 keys?
06:33 Diego Alvarez: negligible CPU, minimal memory. the script is idempotent and we'll provide it.
06:38 Maya Chen: quick check — anyone else tied to procurement timing?
06:41 Ruth Park: procurement is aligned — we need SOW and pricing to move the pilot to a paid POC; payment will be next week if the runbook is accepted.
06:50 Maya Chen: good signal.
06:55 Priya Singh: on the A/B test — how will you signal semantic regressions? a binary pass/fail per prompt?
07:00 Diego Alvarez: we'll compute a similarity score and flag anything under threshold plus manual review for payment prompts.
07:10 Liam O'Connor: ok. one more: do we need a dry run? I'd like to rehearse the canary and cutoff steps without affecting prod.
07:16 Maya Chen: absolutely — propose dry-run with simulated traffic and a small safety window on 2026-10-28.
07:22 Ruth Park: works for us.
07:25 Priya Nair: I'll coordinate with your SRE for the dry-run; will capture timestamps and checklist items.
07:30 Omar Al-Karim: security wants to be present.
07:33 Maya Chen: noted — include sec in the dry-run invite.
07:40 Diego Alvarez: to close — I'll run the extra tail-run and post the CSV by Friday.
07:45 Maya Chen: recap — action items as listed; owners are Diego, Priya N, Maya, Liam, Omar. next meeting same time next week. any final questions?
07:55 Liam O'Connor: none here. thanks team.
08:00 Maya Chen: thanks all, bye.
--- END TRANSCRIPT ---

NOTES: Some speaker labels were generic in the export (Speaker 1). Occasional transcription artifacts: 'K-V cash' for KV cache, 'SLA' sometimes read as 'S-L-A' in transcript. Shared artifacts: security deck link (https://redwood.app/sec/horizon-soc2), runbook draft (https://redwood.app/drive/hz-canary-runbook-draft), benchmark csv (https://redwood.app/drive/hz-24h-tail.csv).
